records.claim: A cryogen-free superconducting 3D vector magnet (6T-1T-1T, 96 mm bore) is a documented magnet option on the Bluefors LD400 (Bluefors Lab Chicago-1 system); this configuration does not include it.

records.location: Section 3.0 'Bluefors Lab Chicago - Facility and Equipment', Chicago-1 System
records.quote: The system is equipped with a cryogen-free superconducting 3D vector magnet with 6T-1T-1T field configuration. The magnet has a 96 mm bore size.
records.reasoning: Bluefors (manufacturer) documents an LD400 delivered with a 3-axis vector magnet; the same 6-1-1 T, 96 mm bore model is in the Bluefors vector-magnet catalog (bluefors.com/products/magnets/vector-magnets/, expanded '3D Vector Magnet Models' list: '6-1-1 Tesla 96 mm bore (~88 mm sample space)'). Vector-field capability therefore exists as a purchasable LD option; this configuration has no magnet, hence optional_not_installed. The LD450 is the renamed LD400; Bluefors states 'the systems themselves remain the same' (rename news, eg_079).

records.claim: A Bluefors LD250 (customized by Bluefors) is documented operating with a dry 9 T superconducting magnet (third-party, Cryomagnetics) in the HAYSTAC axion experiment; this configuration has no magnet.
records.value_as_printed: dry 9T superconducting magnet with a 14 cm diameter cold bore from Cryomagnetics; operation at 60mK in an 8-9T magnetic field
records.document_title: Detecting Dark Matter: The HAYSTAC experiment at Yale University - Bluefors.com
records.location: Section 'Customized Magnet Setup for Further Sensitivity'
records.quote: HAYSTAC is currently using a dry 9T superconducting magnet with a 14 cm diameter cold bore from Cryomagnetics. While the magnet is separately cooled by a Cryomech cryocooler, it ultimately shares a cold space with the LD250 system.
records.reasoning: Manufacturer-hosted customer story: the LD250 'was customized to be compatible with' this magnet (Bluefors engineers adapted flanges and shields). The 2022 LD manual lists 'optional superconducting solenoid magnets' (ev_bf_0041) without a field value. 9 T is the magnet rating (operated at 8-9 T). Caveat: third-party magnet with Bluefors customization, not a Bluefors catalog magnet; treat as a documented-achievable option field, not a standard catalog item.
records.found_via: Tavily search 'HAYSTAC Bluefors LD250 9 T magnet'; verified with tavily_extract. Peer-reviewed HAYSTAC PRL (arXiv 1610.02580) confirms a 9 T Cryomagnetics solenoid but does not name the LD250, so it was not used.

records.claim: The LD dilution refrigerator (LD250/LD400) operates from 7 mK to 4.2 K; the LD450 is the renamed LD400 with unchanged hardware, so its documented range is base (10 mK guaranteed) to 4.2 K.
records.document_title: User Manual LD System, January 12, 2022, Version 2.0 (Bluefors Oy, BF1000-1234517327-9)
records.location: PDF page 6, Section 2.1 General description, first paragraph
records.quote: The cryogen-free dilution refrigerator (DR), with closed helium cycle, is a measurement system for ultra-low temperatures in the range of 7 mK to 4.2 K.
records.reasoning: Same value already used for the LD250/LD400 configurations (ev_bf_0008). Bluefors' March-2026 rename news states 'While we are updating the guaranteed cooling power spec and system names, the systems themselves remain the same.' (https://bluefors.com/news/increased-cooling-power-specifications-for-bluefors-dilution-refrigerators/, eg_079). Lower bound stored as the guaranteed 10 mK base of the LD450 (ev_bf_0010), conservative vs the printed 7 mK and matching the LD400 configuration.
records.found_via: Re-read of the manual (pdftotext) + Tavily extract of the rename news
